the Cut and Count method and the rank based approach can be used to obtain faster randomised and deterministic single exponential time algorithms, respectively polynomial and linear time algorithms, for connectivity problems on planar and other graphs.

(1) the 'Cut and count' method can be applied on branch decompositions, and that (2) representative sets can be used on branch decompositions to obtain a deterministic algorithm for Tsp, that is faster than the fastest known randomised TSP-algorithm.

In summary, our research is concerned with

two main aspects of the dynamic programming paradigm: speeding up algorithms on branch decompositions, and speeding up algorithms on planar inputs, which are both important in the context of the parameterized complexity of problems.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

for planar graphs, the Cut-and-Count method is faster than tree decompositions for the problems mentioned above, while representative sets and Gaussian Elimination is faster than tree decomposition for TSP.
, for planar graphs, the branch decompositions based methods are superior over the tree decompositions based methods, both randomised or deterministic.

the 'Cut and Counter' approach on branch decompositions is faster than the rank based approach on tree decompositions, but the rank based approach is faster than the 'Cut and count' approach on branch decomposition.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
for all the mentioned problems, we obtain faster algorithms on planar and general graphs when the involved weights are polynomial in the number of the vertices.
we can solve these problems in time O(1.5^tw+1.5^b) for planar graphs with O(1) weights on a branch decomposition of width b.
for all these problems, we either obtain the currently fastest algorithms, or we obtain the fastest algorithms for the case that the involved weights are polynomial in the number of nodes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the branch decomposition is a useful tool for dynamic programming algorithms, and that it is often better to use it rather than the tree decomposition.
the Cut and Count method and the rank based approach are not only powerful tools on tree decompositions, but also on branch decompositions.
, in many situations, the branchwidth of a graph is smaller than its treewidth, and that branch decompositions are therefore a good alternative for tree decompositions.
